title: Probabilistic kernel routing + historical prefill profile expansion for more robust benchmarks
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need to expand the benchmark harness so it more accurately reflects production behavior under the runtime's probabilistic kernel routing and varying prefill/decode scheduling strategies. Current golden baselines are brittle when the runtime selects alternate kernels for long-tail sequence lengths or when historical prefill patterns (e.g., multi-turn chats) change the cache hit distribution. This ticket introduces a probabilistic kernel sampler, a historical-prefill profile library, and CI perf gate changes to reduce flaky regressions and surface real regressions earlier.

Goals / success criteria:
- Add a probabilistic kernel-routing emulator to bench harness so each golden run samples kernel choices according to observed production distributions (stochastic sampling seeded for reproducibility).
- Build a curated set of historical prefill profiles (short/long context mixes, multi-prefill patterns, KV cache warm-starts) seeded from production traces anonymized in the last 6 months.
- Create new golden baseline recalibration workflow that supports cohorted baselines (by model family and GPU class) and automated drift detection.
- Define CI perf gates: 95th and 99th quantile latency for synthetic and trace-replay workloads, and median token-throughput; fail CI only on sustained regressions across 3 consecutive runs to avoid flakes.
- Integrate with bench dashboard: expose sampling seed, profile id, and kernel mix for each golden test.

Background / motivation:
We see two recurring issues in perf CI: (1) small kernel selection changes (e.g., fallback to a slower but numerically stable kernel for certain seq-len buckets) cause noisy golden failures even though median production impact is negligible; (2) workloads with different prefill patterns (e.g., many short prefill turns vs. single long prefill) have different batching and KV-cache behavior which shifts latency distributions. The current deterministic harness does not simulate these variations and encourages brittle tuning.

Proposed approach / design:
1) Probabilistic Kernel Sampler:
   - Build a small component in the harness that accepts a kernel-distribution map (kernel_id -> probability) per model+seqlen bucket.
   - The sampler will be seeded from a stable run-id so that CI reruns can reproduce exact kernel choices when investigating failures.
   - Source distributions from recent production telemetry (weekly aggregates). For initial rollout, use synthetic distributions derived from microbench results (e.g., 60/30/10 splits for three dominant kernels in a bucket).

2) Historical Prefill Profile Library:
   - Curate 12 profiles covering dominant customer patterns: chat-heavy (short prefill xN), doc-QA long-prefill, streaming-prefill sequences, and mixed-turn sessions.
   - Each profile encodes: sequence-length histogram for prefill tokens, inter-prefill timing, cache-warm start state, and typical function/tool-calls that influence structured output flows.
   - Profiles will be saved as compact JSON artifacts with a stable id (PROFILE-001 .. PROFILE-012) and metadata: origin, sample size, anonymization tag.

3) Golden Baseline Cohorting and Drift Detection:
   - Instead of one monolithic golden per model, maintain cohorted baselines keyed by (model-family, hardware-class, profile-id).
   - Implement an automated baseline recalibration job that runs nightly to detect drift: if a metric shifts beyond a configurable threshold for 7/7 runs, mark baseline flaky and open an analysis job.

4) CI Perf Gate Rules:
   - Gate metrics: p95 latency, p99 latency, median tokens/sec, and a custom "kv-cache-miss-rate" proxy.
   - Use a rolling triage policy: a single CI failure flags a perf alert but does not block; three consecutive failures within 48h will block the release branch.
   - Include noise filtering: require delta > noise-floor (determined by baseline variance) before counting as a regression.

5) Observability / Artifacts:
   - Record and surface: sampling seed, profile id, kernel-distribution vector, raw traces for failed runs, and microkernel microbench scores.
   - Add a bench-run summary to the console dashboard and link to the trace replay dashboard for deep dives.

Planned experiments and timeline:
- Week 1 (Feb 18–24): implement probabilistic sampler and seed mechanics; add feature flags.
- Week 2 (Feb 25–Mar 3): ingest synthetic kernel-distribution maps, implement profile JSON schema, and add two initial profiles (chat-short, long-doc).
- Week 3 (Mar 4–10): run ensemble of golden runs to collect variance; produce initial cohorted baselines for two model families on A100 and T4.
- Week 4 (Mar 11–17): implement CI gate rules and noise-floor calculation; create dashboard summaries.
- Week 5 (Mar 18–24): iterate on profile set (expand to 8), calibrate thresholds, and ship runtime-1.20 perf gating.

Progress updates / notes:
- 2025-02-19: Prototype sampler implemented (branch: feat/bench/prob-sampler). Verified seed-based determinism locally (seed reproduces kernel choices across runs).
- 2025-02-27: Profile schema PR opened (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/412). Added PROFILE-001 (chat-short) and PROFILE-002 (doc-long) to S3 test artifacts.
- 2025-03-03: Initial golden ensemble completed for small model family on A100. Observed p95 variance increase of ~4% versus deterministic runs; p50 unchanged. This suggests kernel mixing increases tail noise—will refine noise-floor.

Review feedback / trade-offs:
- PM (Liam Chen): prefer conservative CI gating initially — make first failures only alerting (non-blocking) for two weeks.
- Design (Maya Rivera): dashboard needs explicit visualization for kernel-mix to help on-call correlate regressions to kernel shifts.
- Eng (SRE) concern: storing raw production traces requires extra anonymization and access controls; plan to use aggregated histograms for kernel-distribution seeding and only synthetic replay traces in public CI.

Open questions / blockers:
- Need final sign-off on which production telemetry tables are allowed to seed kernel distributions (privacy / compliance). Owner: Security & Compliance.
- Determine noise-floor computation: use bootstrapped CI on historical golden runs or set fixed-percent thresholds per metric. Action: run bootstrapped analysis job (ENG-43912-bstrap).

Follow-ups / next tickets:
- ENG-43913: expand profile library to 12 canonical profiles and add tooling to auto-generate profiles from anonymized traces.
- ENG-43914: integrate kv-cache-miss instrumentation into bench harness for more accurate cache-rate metrics.

Artifacts / links:
- PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/412 (profile schema)
- Feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/tree/feat/bench/prob-sampler
- Dashboard mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/bench-dashboard-mock (internal)
- Initial golden run results: s3://redwood-bench/golden-runs/ENG-43912/2025-03-03/summary.csv

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Probabilistic sampler merged behind a feature flag and exercised in nightly harness.
- At least 4 prefill profiles present; cohorted baselines created for two model families across two hardware classes.
- CI perf gate rules implemented and documented; noise-floor and triage policy described in the runbook.
- Dashboard surfaces sampling metadata and links to raw traces for failed runs.

Owner notes:
- Keep the initial seed-to-baseline mapping stable (store seeds with run metadata). When investigating regressions, we should be able to re-run the exact kernel sequence that produced the failure.
- Emphasize reproducibility over randomness for debugging; sampling randomness is only for simulating production variation in nightly/golden runs, not necessarily for presubmit CI unless flagged as experimental.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for sampler determinism (same seed -> same sequence).
- Integration test that runs each profile and verifies artifact creation (profile-id in bench metadata).
- Backfill job to compute baseline variance using 30 historical runs to set noise-floor per metric.

Estimated risk level: medium (introduces noise into golden runs which can increase triage load initially).

If blocked, fallback plan:
- Revert to deterministic harness and instead attach synthetic perturbations deterministically (rotate kernel choices with a fixed schedule) until profile ingestion and noise-floor tuning are stable.

Contact for context: Rohit Kapoor (assignee), Ava Martinez (creator), and Liam Chen (PM).
